page.layout: One page of text in a single column; marginal notes in the right margin (Prosyllogismus, Epilogismus, Prosyllogismus marks); a fragment of the facing left page with margin notes at the left edge, not transcribed as it is the neighbouring page's edge.

main_text.p: Consequentia igitur syllogismi, propter aequivocationis sophisma, est prorsus nulla.
III. Si ex dogmate de Satisfactione consequitur, nobis in aeternū pereundum esse: illud utique dogma, nostri respectu, perniciosum quiddam statuit, At prius. Ergo & posterius:Prosyllo-gismus III.
main_text.head: Assumtionis probatio.
main_text.p: Ex quo dogmate sequitur, Christum ex mortuis non resurrexisse; ex eodem etiam consequitur, nobis in aeternum pereundum esse. Quoniam, si Christus non resurrexit: vana est fides nostra, & nos adhuc sumus in peccatis nostris; quibus aeternum exitiū debetur. 1. Cor. 15. v. 17.Epilogismus.
Ex dogmate autem, de Satisfactione Christi pro peccatis nostris, sequitur, Christum ex mortuis non resurrexisse.
Ergo ex eodem dogmate de Satisfactione consequitur, nobis in aeternum pereundum esse.
main_text.head: Minor huius Epilogismi sic probatur.
main_text.p: Ex dogmate, statuente Christum aeternam mortem subiisse, sequitur, eundem a mortuis non resurrexisse.Prosyllo-gismus

page.notes: Marginal notes are small and partly cut; the note labels are read approximately. The left-edge text belongs to the facing page and is omitted. Several words in the margin notes and the catchword are uncertain.
